title: M1/M2/M7: the command bar cannot find live sessions that wait on the user — `/jump kestrel` answers "No session matches" while kestrel sits at its permission prompt; with no name it picks a done session
repro: Fleet: kestrel at its permission prompt, beacon at its AskUserQuestion, vibepet done (all idle in tmux)
Type `/jump kestrel` ⏎, then `/jump beacon` ⏎, `/jump vibepet` ⏎, `/replay beacon` ⏎
Re-arm kestrel into a fresh approval; at 35–97 s `/jump deploy` matches it (shown as running); at 138 s type `/jump deploy` ⏎ again
With kestrel and beacon blocked (shown running) type `/jump` ⏎ with no name
expected: The bar resolves every live session of the fleet by name or title (Claude Code's registry knows them all), and with no name targets the session that needs the user first.
actual: "No session matches “kestrel”." (also beacon, vibepet) — identical to a nonexistent name ("zebra"). `/jump deploy` matched at 01:55Z but at 138 s into the same wait said "No session matches “deploy”."; `/replay beacon` said no match while the Theater… menu listed "Beacon database choice · beacon · 10m". `/jump` with no name jumped to vibepet (done) while kestrel and beacon were blocked. The bar only searches the sessions Home shows, and Home drops or mislabels blocked ones.
truth: kestrel registry waiting(permission prompt) 4665 s (01:50Z) and 138 s into a fresh wait (01:56:58Z); beacon waiting(input needed) 4662 s and 621 s; vibepet idle (turn done, statement) 2976 s

title: M11: `/jump <session>` never reaches a tmux session (22/22 failed) and overwrites the clipboard with `claude --resume <id>` for a session that is still live

expected: The session's tmux pane is brought forward (the registry names the pane), or the panel says exactly why not and offers a working next step; never a clipboard command that would start a second claude on a live session.
actual: 22 of 22 `/jump` runs returned ok:false after 100–281 ms (median 141); every one wrote `cd ~/.vibepet-ultra/fleet/<repo> && claude --resume <session id>` to the clipboard. The user is left to find the pane by hand.

title: CH27: no /approve, /deny, /reply or /answer — a blocked session cannot be resolved from the command bar
repro: Fleet: kestrel at its permission prompt, beacon at its AskUserQuestion
Open Home; type `/approve kestrel` ⏎, `/deny kestrel` ⏎, `/reply beacon Postgres` ⏎, `/answer beacon 2` ⏎

title: Ambiguous names resolve silently to one session: `/jump a` → vibepet (3 matches), `/replay run` → atlas; the tie-break follows a clock that restarts every tick (M4)
repro: Rows: vibepet "Read package.json" (ready), ember (ready), beacon "Beacon database choice", kestrel "Deploy.sh dry run", atlas "Run build.sh" (running)

expected: With several matches the bar lists them (or asks which), and never acts on a pick the user cannot predict.

"run" matches kestrel and atlas: at 01:55:15Z the bar's matcher ranked kestrel first, from 01:55:38Z all 9 real runs went to atlas — its row clock restarts every few seconds ("atlas · 0s"), making it the newest. `/replay run` opened "Theater — atlas".
truth: kestrel waiting(permission prompt) 35–97 s and beacon waiting(input needed) 35–97 s (both shown as running); atlas busy (build.sh) 82–147 s; vibepet idle (done) 13–35 s
